title: On Regarding the matter as a warning
subtitle: 价值观 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 价值观（做人与做事·价值观与人生意义）
meta: 主题语境：价值观（做人与做事·价值观与人生意义）　|　核心词汇：regard　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 regard 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1991 the keeper ① regarded the matter as a warning twice over, and every traveller in the tower said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the keeper ② regards the matter as a warning year after year without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ regard the matter as a warning at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ regarded the matter as a warning before — a line in the calendar for January 1985 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Regarding the matter as a warning twice over, the keeper said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the clock at the far stair, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ regard the stranger with great care year after year, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Regard the stranger with great care at once and never mention it again.

By 1998 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the calendar, and a new traveller from the next tower ⑧ regards the stranger with great care twice over every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stair, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ regarded the matter as a warning again when nobody else would.

⑩ To regard the matter as a warning, my mother said in 2003, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the tower remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the tower forgets, somebody regards the matter as a warning year after year again and somebody must regard the matter as a warning twice over all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 看待（一般过去式 regarded the matter as a warning：1991 年守夜人头一回这样做，来回两遍）
B. v. 看待（一般现在 regards the matter as a warning：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 看待（不定式 to regard the matter as a warning：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 看待（过去完成时 had regarded the matter as a warning：1985 年一月的年历上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 看待（动名词 regarding the matter as a warning 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 注视（regard the stranger with great care：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去注视把那位生人打量了很久）
G. v. 注视（regard the stranger with great care：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 看待（后段两处：新来的过路人照例 regards the stranger with great care，而母亲又一次 regarded the matter as a warning）

answers.why: regard 意为“看待”，1991 年守夜人来回两遍看待把这件事看成一次警告，那是钟楼里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 regarded。
regard 意为“看待”，自那以后守夜人年年地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 regards。
regard 意为“看待”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯看待把这件事看成一次警告”，此处为不定式 to regard the matter as a warning。
regard 意为“看待”，年历里 一月 那行字说明早在 1998 年之前就有人看待过，故用过去完成时 had regarded。
regard 意为“看待”，守夜人说“看待把这件事看成一次警告这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 regarding the matter as a warning 作主语。
regard 意为“注视”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去注视把那位生人打量了很久”，should ever 之后用原形 regard the stranger with great care。
regard 意为“注视”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻注视把那位生人打量了很久（regard the stranger with great care at once），以后再也不要提起。
regard 意为“看待”，新来的过路人每个年头都照例注视把那位生人打量了很久，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 regards。
regard 意为“看待”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次来回两遍看待把这件事看成一次警告，用一般过去式 regarded 叙述。
regard 意为“看待”，结尾那句是母亲 2003 年的话：要看待把这件事看成一次警告，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和钟楼记住的那一件。

多年以后，守夜人仍年年地做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（regards the matter as a warning）

守夜人说过，来回两遍看待把这件事看成一次警告这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（regarding the matter as a warning 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻注视把那位生人打量了很久，以后再也不要提起。（regard the stranger with great care，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 regard 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1991 the keeper regarded the matter as a warning twice over, and nobody in the tower forgot it.
Even now the keeper regards the matter as a warning year after year whenever the tower asks.
Regarding the matter as a warning twice over, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever regard the stranger with great care year after year, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new traveller from the next tower regards the stranger with great care twice over every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother regarded the matter as a warning again, and the tower remembered that half.
